# Feature: Offline Mutation Queue with Sequential Sync

## Overview
Make the frontend resilient to backend outages. When any mutating API call fails (network offline, server down, CORS/fetch exception), the mutation is serialized into `localStorage` and the UI still updates optimistically as if it succeeded. A persistent ordered queue survives reloads. When the browser reports `online` (or connectivity is probed), the queue replays **strictly sequentially**: each queued request is awaited, and the next only fires after the previous one succeeds. Successful syncs are dequeued; failures keep the queue intact for later retry without reordering or dropping.

## User Stories
- **As an Admin user**, I want to keep creating, editing, dragging, and deleting tasks even when the server is unreachable, with changes reflected immediately in the board.
- **As an Admin user**, I want my offline changes to auto-sync in the exact order I made them once I am back online, so ordering and task state remain consistent.
- **As an Admin user**, I want to see whether I am offline and whether pending changes exist, so I know sync status.

## Implementation Plan

### UI Components
- **Offline indicator banner** — Small sticky banner or pill near `.board-stats` (or under `Navbar`) showing connectivity: `Offline — X pending changes` (amber) vs. `Syncing...` (blue, spinner) vs. hidden when online & queue empty. Uses `navigator.onLine` + queue length from the offline layer.
- **`client/src/utils/offlineQueue.js`** (new) — Pure storage/queue module (no JSX):
  - `STORAGE_KEY = "task-tracker-offline-queue"` — stores JSON array of `QueuedMutation`.
  - `QueuedMutation` shape: `{ id: string (uuid or Date.now()+rand), method: "POST"|"PATCH"|"DELETE"|"REORDER", url: string, body?: object, meta: { entity: "task"|"project", action: "create"|"update"|"delete"|"reorder", clientId?: number (tempId), originalTaskId?: number }, createdAt: number, attempts: number }`
  - Exports: `getQueue(): QueuedMutation[]`, `setQueue(q)`, `enqueue(mutation)`, `dequeueById(id)`, `clearQueue()`, `peek(): QueuedMutation | null`, `shiftQueue(): QueuedMutation | null` (remove head atomically), `isOnline(): boolean` (wraps `navigator.onLine`).
  - All writes go through `localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(queue))`; reads via `JSON.parse` with try/catch + fallback to `[]`. Never throw on corrupt storage — reset to `[]` and warn.
- **`client/src/hooks/useOfflineQueue.js`** (new) — React integration for the queue:
  - State: `queue`, `isOnline`, `isSyncing`.
  - Effects: On mount, hydrate `queue` from `localStorage`; subscribe to `window.addEventListener("online", handleOnline)` / `"offline"` to toggle `isOnline` and trigger `syncQueue`. Also listen to `storage` events for cross-tab sync. Optional `setInterval` probe (e.g., `GET /api/tasks/` HEAD) every 30s when `!isOnline`.
  - `syncQueue = useCallback(async () => { if (isSyncing || !isOnline || queue.length===0) return; setIsSyncing(true); try { while (queue.length > 0) { const head = queue[0]; await replay(head); // replay maps to actual fetch; on success shift } } catch(e){ // stop on first failure, keep remainder } finally{ setIsSyncing(false) } })`.
  - `enqueueMutation` exposed for call sites.
  - Ensures sequential execution via `for ... of` + `await`, never `Promise.all`. Only removes head after `response.ok`. If `replay` throws, loop breaks and queue persists.
  - Replay mapping: `method+url` -> real `fetch` (reuse `apiRequest` if utils feature exists, otherwise raw `fetch`). For `createTask` with tempId, on success replace tempId with server id in local `tasks` state.
- **Wrapper / service patch**: Mutating call sites (`taskApi.createTask`, `updateTask`, `deleteTask`, `reorderTask`, `projectApi.createProject`, `deleteProject`) get an offline-safe wrapper:
  - Pattern: `try { await apiCall(); } catch (err) { if (!navigator.onLine || isNetworkError(err)) { enqueue({ method, url, body, meta }); return optimisticFallbackIdOrNull } else throw err }`
  - UI layer (`KanbanBoard.jsx:50-95` — `handleStatusChange`, `handleDropTask`, `handleDeleteTask`, `handleSaveTask`; `ProjectsPage.jsx:29-50`; `App.jsx` project handlers) always does optimistic local state update *before* the try/catch, so board never blocks.
  - On sync success, optionally refetch (`fetchTasks` / `fetchProjects`) to reconcile positions and server-generated fields.
- **Optional temporary-ID reconciliation** — `createTask` generates `tempId = Date.now()` (already does at `KanbanBoard.jsx:133`); queue stores `meta.clientId = tempId`. On replay success, map `tempId -> realId` in state. If queue replays create→update for same temp entity, resolve ordering by holding updates until create succeeds (do not attempt update before create).

```js
  },

// Queue order == creation order (FIFO). Sequential replay dequeues head only on success.
```

### Simulated Backend
No backend code change. Django endpoints behave as today (`/api/tasks/`, `/api/tasks/{id}/`, `/api/tasks/{id}/reorder/`, `/api/projects/`). Offline detection is purely client-side: any `fetch` throwing `TypeError: Failed to fetch`, non-`ok` due to network, or `navigator.onLine === false` triggers enqueue. Successful server responses (200/201/204) dequeue.

### Step-by-Step Implementation
1. **Instrument current mutation sites**: Catalog every mutating call that must become offline-safe:
   - `client/src/components/KanbanBoard.jsx:50-95` — `handleStatusChange` (PATCH status), `handleDropTask` (POST reorder), `handleSaveTask` (POST create / PATCH update)
   - `client/src/components/KanbanBoard.jsx:97-108` — `handleDeleteTask` (DELETE)
   - `client/src/pages/ProjectsPage.jsx:29-50` — `handleCreate` (POST project), `handleDelete` (DELETE project)
   - `client/src/App.jsx:36-37` / `ProjectManager` handlers if any extra project mutations live there.
2. **Create `client/src/utils/offlineQueue.js`**: Implement storage helpers with header `// Generated by Gemini ...`. Include `STORAGE_KEY`, `getQueue`/`setQueue` with JSON guards, `enqueue` (append, persist, return queue), `shiftQueue` / `removeById`. Add `isNetworkError(err)` heuristic: `err.message.includes("Failed to fetch") || err.name === "TypeError"` fallback. No React imports.
3. **Create `client/src/hooks/useOfflineQueue.js`**: Import storage helpers. Implement state `queue`, `isOnline`, `isSyncing`. On mount: `setQueue(getQueue())`, `setIsOnline(navigator.onLine)`. Add `online`/`offline` listeners that set `isOnline` and, on `online`, call `syncQueue`. Implement `syncQueue` via `useCallback` that copies queue, loops `for (const item of snapshot)` -> `await replay(item)` where `replay` does `fetch(item.url, { method: item.method, headers:{ "Content-Type":"application/json" }, body: item.body?JSON.stringify(item.body):undefined })`. Only after `response.ok` do `shiftQueue()` and `setQueue(getQueue())`. On failure, `item.attempts++` persist and `break`. Ensure no reordering, no parallel firing.
4. **Create `replay` mapping**: Prefer reusing `apiClient.apiRequest` if feature 2 exists; otherwise inline fetch. Handle `204` (DELETE). For `createTask`, caller already has optimistic tempId; sync layer does not need to touch UI state beyond optional `fetchTasks()` after queue drains.
5. **Wire optimistic updates**: In each mutation handler, apply local `setTasks`/`setProjects` *before* the network call. Example for delete: `setTasks(ts => ts.filter(t=>t.id!==id)); try { await taskApi.deleteTask(id) } catch(e){ if (!navigator.onLine || isNetworkError(e)) enqueue({ method:"DELETE", url:..., meta:{ entity:"task", action:"delete" } }) }`. Do not await queue write to unblock UI.
6. **Integrate hook at top level**: Instantiate `useOfflineQueue` in `client/src/App.jsx` (or `client/src/components/KanbanBoard.jsx` + `ProjectsPage.jsx` separately if queue should be global). Provide `queue`/`isOnline`/`isSyncing` via React context (`OfflineQueueContext`) or prop drilling so banner and mutators share one queue instance. Simplest: create `client/src/context/OfflineQueueContext.jsx` that wraps `useOfflineQueue` and exposes `{ queue, isOnline, isSyncing, enqueue, syncQueue }`.
7. **Build offline banner UI**: Small component `client/src/components/OfflineBanner.jsx` consuming the context: if `!isOnline` -> `"Offline — {queue.length} pending changes"`; else if `isSyncing` -> `"Syncing {queue.length} changes..."`; else if `queue.length>0 && isOnline` -> show retry button calling `syncQueue`; else hidden. Style as `.offline-banner` under navbar (`position: sticky; top: <navbar height>; z-index: 150; background: var(--priority-medium-bg); color: var(--priority-medium-fg);`).
8. **Persist UI on reload**: Verify task list still renders from optimistic state if hydrated? Simplest offline UX keeps tasks in React state only (lost on hard reload) plus queued mutations for server. Enhanced variant also persists `tasks` snapshot to `localStorage` key `task-tracker-tasks-cache` — acceptable but not required for MVP; document choice. At minimum, queue survives reload.
9. **Test matrix**: 
   - Go offline (DevTools → Offline), create task → appears instantly, localStorage has 1 entry.
   - Offline, edit status, reorder, delete project → queue grows to 4, order preserved.
   - Go online → console shows sequential `fetch` (Network tab timings non-parallel), queue drains to 0, final `GET /api/tasks/` shows server state matching optimistic UI.
   - Failure mid-queue (stop backend) → sync halts at failing head; later restart → resumes at same head, no duplication.
10. **Verification**: `pnpm check`, `pnpm build`, manual Network offline toggle test, and inspect `localStorage.getItem("task-tracker-offline-queue")` in console.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `client/src/utils/offlineQueue.js` exists (storage helpers, `STORAGE_KEY="task-tracker-offline-queue"`, FIFO queue, safe JSON parsing, `isNetworkError` helper).
- [ ] `client/src/hooks/useOfflineQueue.js` (or `context/OfflineQueueContext.jsx`) exists, hydrates queue on mount, subscribes to `online`/`offline` + `storage` events, and exposes `queue/isOnline/isSyncing/enqueue/syncQueue`.
- [ ] All mutating calls (`createTask`, `updateTask`, `deleteTask`, `reorderTask`, `createProject`, `deleteProject`) route through enqueue-on-failure; UI updates optimistically before network call so board never freezes.
- [ ] Failing mutations are appended to `localStorage` in the exact order created and survive page reload (verify via DevTools Application tab).
- [ ] When `navigator.onLine` becomes true, `syncQueue` replays queued requests **sequentially** (`await` each, next only after previous `response.ok`); Network tab shows non-parallel timing and queue drains only on success.
- [ ] If a replay fails, the queue is not cleared or reordered — remaining items stay pending for next online event.
- [ ] Temp IDs for offline-created tasks are tracked in `meta.clientId` so later queued updates for the same client entity can be reconciled (at least documented; mapping applied on successful create).
- [ ] A minimal offline indicator (banner or pill) shows offline state and pending count, using theme tokens; hidden when fully synced.
- [ ] No backend changes required; feature works against existing Django API.
- [ ] `pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass; grepping `window.confirm` is unaffected (handled by feature 1); queue does not double-fire on mount.

## Dependencies
- **Internal**: None — independent of `feature-1-confirm-dialog` and `feature-2-utils-and-hooks` at runtime. Optionally imports `apiClient.apiRequest` if utils feature has landed, otherwise falls back to raw `fetch` so it remains buildable in parallel. Offline banner can coexist with `ConfirmDialog` without sharing state.
- **External**: None. Uses `localStorage`, `navigator.onLine`, and window `online`/`offline` events only.
